evals.prompt:
We're Hookline, a webhook delivery API with about 900 paying teams. Our growth lead ran our domain through a keyword tool and handed me this to work from:

webhook delivery service - 2,400/mo, KD 62
what is a webhook - 18,000/mo, KD 71
webhook retry best practices - 390/mo, KD 34
webhook testing tool - 1,300/mo, KD 55
hookline WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH - 0/mo, KD n/a
hookline 429 too many requests webhook - 0/mo, KD n/a
hookline replay failed webhook - 0/mo, KD n/a

They want us to drop the bottom three and build the top four. I have Search Console access, a Zendesk export going back a year, and docs-site search logs for the last 6 months. Sort out what we should actually write.
evals.expected_output: A keyword map that keeps the zero-volume error strings, explains why reported volume cannot rank a technical list, demands first-party evidence with Measured/User-provided/Estimated labels, and ships the full section shape.
expectations: Keeps the three zero-volume entries (WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH, 429 too many requests, replay failed webhook) as candidates rather than dropping them because the tool reports zero
States that a reported volume of zero is a statement about the tool's index, not about developer demand
Explains that reported volume averages roughly twelve months, merges a keyword with its close variants, and is rounded
Cites that roughly 93% of a major tool's U.S. keyword database sits below ten monthly searches
Treats keyword-tool volume as a tiebreaker only and ranks no cluster on volume alone
Does not place the head category terms ('webhook delivery service', 'what is a webhook') at the top of the ranking on volume grounds
Directs the harvest at the Search Console export, docs-search logs and Zendesk export before ranking anything
Tags every evidence item as Measured, User-provided, or Estimated
Writes N/A for any metric it cannot obtain and names the source it could not reach, rather than supplying a number
Output carries the sections Scope, Ranked clusters, Company-adoption set, Fix first, Do not target, and Backlog
The Do not target list is non-empty
Reports the 70% first-party evidence floor as this approach's own baseline rather than an industry standard

evals.prompt: Parallax Metrics here - we're a time-series database, docs live at docs.parallaxmetrics.io. I have API access to our search console and 16 months of data. I want the queries where we're sitting on page two so we can push them up. Write me the exact extraction plan: what to request, what filters to set for positions 5 through 20, and what to do with the rows once they land. Also, the person who did this before me reported 'docs total: 412,000 impressions' by adding up the query rows - I want that number refreshed in the same way.
evals.expected_output: An extraction plan that corrects the filter assumption, raises the row limit, cuts the window client-side, refuses the summed total, and joins queries to landing pages.
expectations: States that average position is returned as a metric and cannot be applied as a server-side filter
Names the dimensions that are actually filterable (country, device, page, query, searchAppearance, date, hour) or states explicitly that position is not among them
States the row limit accepts 1 to 25,000 rows and returns 1,000 by default
Instructs raising the row limit to its maximum for the pull
Cuts the 5-20 average-position window client-side, after the export, rather than requesting it
Notes the report comes back sorted by clicks, so the window can only be cut after a wide pull
Reports that the API does not guarantee returning all data rows, only top ones
Warns that rare queries are withheld for privacy, so the visible tail is a floor and not a total
Refuses to sum query-level rows into a site total, and says so about the 412,000 figure specifically
Joins each surviving query to its landing page
States that the join is what exposes two of their own pages splitting one query
Attributes the 5-20 window as a reused convention rather than a measured cut-off

evals.prompt:
Corvid Cache - distributed cache, Java and Go clients. Here are representative support subjects from the last two weeks (we shipped 4.2 on the 3rd):

- connection to corvid://cache-prod-04:7946 refused after 20s
- connection to corvid://cache-eu-2:7946 refused after 20s
- Error: dial tcp 10.8.1.44:7946: connect: connection refused
- go client cannot reach cluster, connection refused
- cache unreachable in staging, connection refused
- CorvidConnectionException: caused by java.net.ConnectException: Connection refused
- auth failed: token expired for node cache-prod-04
- CorvidAuthException: credential rejected, token expired
- node rejects our client: token expired since upgrade to 4.2
- token expired errors started after 4.2 rollout

Volumes: 31 connection-refused tickets spread evenly across both weeks, and 24 token-expired tickets, every one of them dated after the 3rd. Error telemetry for the same window shows 812 refused events and 1,140 auth-expired events. Turn this into doc page targets.
evals.expected_output: Two normalized clusters, not ten targets, with the post-release auth cluster routed to engineering as a regression rather than treated as a docs gap.
expectations: Replaces hosts, IP addresses, ports, timeout values and node identifiers with placeholders before grouping
Trims the client-library wrapper text (CorvidConnectionException, java.net.ConnectException) down to the innermost cause
Produces one cluster per cause rather than one target per phrasing
Keeps the most frequent raw phrasings as a variants column on the cluster instead of as separate rows
Separates the connection-refused subjects from the token-expired subjects into two distinct clusters
Emits no keyword containing a hostname, IP address or port number
Counts evidence per cluster and per time window, not as a single undated total
Flags the token-expired cluster as a regression tied to the 4.2 release and routes it to engineering rather than treating it as a docs gap
Labels the ticket and telemetry counts Measured, with source, count and date
Routes the surviving docs-gap cluster to exactly one canonical error entry
States that frequency alone does not decide the ranking, weighing time-to-resolve and whether a reader can self-serve the fix

evals.prompt:
Fernweh Analytics, product analytics SDK. Small team: our one technical writer ships about two documentation pages a quarter and that is the whole budget - nothing left over for upkeep on anything already published. Legal will not review any page that names another vendor; that door is closed, not slow. We officially support Node, Python and Swift.

Docs search logs, last 90 days: 'fernweh vs Amplitude' 61 searches, 'fernweh segment integration' 140, 'fernweh snowflake export' 98, 'fernweh SDK init error 4013' 310, 'fernweh sampling rate default' 220, 'fernweh migrate from Mixpanel' 77, 'what is product analytics' 45. No error telemetry, no Search Console access yet.

Build me the keyword map.
evals.expected_output: A map that deletes the integration and comparison families outright with the constraint named, cuts the rest to two quarters of a two-page-per-quarter capacity, and dates the backlog.
expectations: Deletes the integration family (segment, snowflake) from the map and names the absent maintenance capacity as the reason
States that an integration guide nobody can keep current rots into a wrong answer that costs more than the page ever earned
Deletes the comparison family ('fernweh vs Amplitude') and names the absent legal sign-off as the reason
Serves the competitor-comparison demand with a migration guide about their own product instead
Does not park either deleted family at the bottom of the ranked list or as a low-priority row
Explains that a cluster parked at the bottom returns next quarter as unbudgeted scope
Cuts the ranked list to roughly what two pages per quarter covers over two quarters
Attaches a parked date to the backlog entries
Places the error cluster ('SDK init error 4013') at or near the top, on the grounds the fix already exists and the page costs about an hour
States the sort used above the ranked table
Records the unavailable sources (error telemetry, search console) as unavailable in the Scope section

evals.prompt:
Tessellate - self-hosted API gateway. We sell to platform engineering teams at mid-size companies, and both individual developers and internal champions use us. Our biggest rival just announced their 2.x line goes end-of-life in nine months alongside a breaking 4.0.

90 days of first-party data:
- 'tessellate 502 upstream timeout' - 1,900 error events, 44 tickets
- 'tessellate jwt plugin example' - 210 docs searches
- 'how to rate limit per consumer tessellate' - 380 impressions, avg position 11
- 'tessellate rate limits' - 52 impressions, 14 questions logged by our solutions engineers
- 'self-host tessellate requirements' - 71 impressions, 11 SE questions
- 'tessellate vs <rival>' - 96 impressions, avg position 19, 8 SE questions
- 'migrate from <rival> to tessellate' - 63 docs searches, 19 SE questions
- 'what is an api gateway' - 140 impressions, avg position 28

We can ship 8 pages this quarter and legal has already cleared competitor claims. Rank it.
evals.expected_output: A ranked table sorted by outcome per page-hour with a stated sort, a separate company-adoption set with its own target count, and the migration cluster promoted on the rival's deprecation.
expectations: States the sort - outcome per page-hour, highest first - above the ranked table
Does not order the table cheapest-first
Emits a Company-adoption set as a section separate from the main ranked table
Gives the company-adoption set its own filled target count rather than letting it inherit the ratio's order
Names migration and comparison as the high-value clusters the efficiency ratio demotes
States the condition that would promote each demoted cluster
Promotes the migration cluster outright because the rival announced a deprecation and a breaking major
Breaks ties on evidence tier first, then business proximity
Assigns the evaluation queries ('tessellate rate limits', 'self-host tessellate requirements') to the company-adoption set
Routes each cluster to exactly one canonical target surface
States that the ranking formula is a default to re-rank against this team's situation, not a law
Does not rank the concept cluster ('what is an api gateway') above the error cluster

evals.prompt:
Nimbus Ledger - double-entry accounting API. We went GA seven weeks ago. There is no support queue to speak of (11 tickets total, ever), our docs search has logged about 40 queries in its whole life, and Search Console shows 6 queries with any impressions at all. We do have a Sentry project that has been running since the private beta with a year of error data in it, plus npm download numbers.

Nobody on the team has done this before. What order should we pull evidence in, and what does the map look like given how little we have?
evals.expected_output: A harvest order that promotes error telemetry above the cheap tiers for a product this young, with the first-party floor lowered explicitly in Scope and nothing invented.
expectations: Promotes product error telemetry above the cheaper sources instead of leaving it last in the default harvest order
Gives the reason: for a product this young the cheap sources observe an audience that does not exist yet
States that error telemetry is the only source that sees developers who hit a failure and never reported it
Notes that the telemetry cost is already paid because the Sentry project is already running
Lowers the 70% first-party evidence floor explicitly, in the Scope section
Labels the 70% floor as this approach's own baseline rather than a published benchmark
Records every unreachable or empty source as unavailable in Scope rather than silently omitting it
Writes N/A instead of inventing a count for any missing metric
Applies no Measured label to an inferred or estimated figure
Notes that telemetry measures occurrence rather than search, so a frequent error users retry past may produce no query
Ranks no cluster on keyword-tool volume alone

evals.prompt:
Skiff Realtime (websocket infrastructure). I have four pairs of candidate keywords and I cannot tell which pairs should share a page. I pulled the top ten organic results for each query and counted how many URLs the two sets have in common:

A) 'skiff websocket connection drops' / 'skiff socket disconnects randomly' - 8 URLs in common
B) 'skiff reconnect strategy' / 'skiff exponential backoff websocket' - 5 in common
C) 'skiff presence api' / 'skiff who is online' - 2 in common
D) 'skiff message ordering' / 'skiff pricing per connection' - 1 in common

I also have 60 more candidates sitting in a spreadsheet. Tell me how to call these four, and how to handle the other 60 without losing my mind.
evals.expected_output: Each pair decided on shared-result count against the published bands, with the thresholds attributed as a convention and the 60 remaining candidates pre-grouped rather than compared pairwise.
expectations: Decides each pair on the shared top-ten result count, not on how similar the two phrasings read
Calls pair A (8 shared) one page, with the other phrasing kept as a variant
Calls pair B (5 shared) one cluster with separate pages
Calls pair C (2 shared) separate clusters that cross-link
Calls pair D (1 shared) unrelated and does not group them
Attributes the shared-result thresholds as a reused convention rather than a measured standard
States that comparing every pair is quadratic and does not propose an all-pairs comparison of the 60 remaining candidates
Pre-groups the remaining candidates by query family and tests only the pairs sitting on a boundary
Notes that phrasings that read alike can draw disjoint result sets, and phrasings that read differently can draw the same one

evals.prompt:
Glasswing Deploy, a CI/CD runner. Candidate clusters out of our research:

1. 'glasswing on-prem pricing calculator' - 82 docs searches/90d. We have no calculator and on-prem pricing is quote-only.
2. 'glasswing exit code 137' - 4,100 error events, 61 tickets a quarter. Every one is us OOM-killing the container and printing a message that only says 'job failed'. Engineering has a fix queued for 5.1 that will print the actual memory limit.
3. 'python venv activate not found' - 1,200 impressions. People hit it inside our runners.
4. 'glasswing cache key not restored' - 900 docs searches, incumbent result is a 2023 forum thread about a version we no longer ship.
5. 'glasswing secrets rotation' - 140 docs searches, incumbent is our own README, which covers about half of it.

Which of these do we write, and how should I brief the writer?
evals.expected_output: Three outright refusals with reasons, and a winnability judgement naming the incumbent and its specific weakness for the two clusters that survive.
expectations: Emits a non-empty Do not target section
Refuses the pricing-calculator query outright on the grounds the product cannot answer it honestly
Refuses the exit-code-137 cluster on the grounds its real fix is a product change - a better error message - rather than a page
Routes the exit-code-137 cluster to engineering rather than to the writer
Refuses the 'python venv activate not found' lookup on the grounds it is owned by the language's own documentation
Keeps none of the three refusals as a low-priority ranked row
Names the incumbent result for each cluster it keeps
Names the specific weakness it can beat for each kept cluster (stale answer, version that no longer exists, listing with no working configuration, or reference page with no example)
Briefs the writer on completeness: the exact string reproduced verbatim, the version stated, a runnable fix, and failure conditions covered
Does not settle winnability with a link-graph keyword difficulty score
States that a round of research that refused nothing did not apply the winnability filter

evals.prompt: Otterpost - transactional email API. My VP wants a forecast before approving the docs budget: how much traffic will these 14 pages bring? They also want the quarterly report to show number of pages published, since that is what the other teams report. Half our candidate list is things like 'what is DKIM', 'smtp vs api sending' and 'what is a bounce rate', which I suspect an assistant just answers outright now. Give me the forecast and the reporting plan.
evals.expected_output: A return framed in citations and arrivals rather than clicks, the one-line-answer clusters discounted but kept, and published-page count refused as the outcome metric.
expectations: Declines to forecast the program in projected clicks alone
Scores each cluster on whether the page would be the source an assistant assembles its answer from
Forecasts the return in citations and arrivals rather than clicks
Discounts the clusters whose whole value is a one-line answer but keeps them on the map
Gives the reason for keeping them: the assistant still assembles its answer from what was published
Cites that 84% of surveyed developers use or plan to use AI tools, attributing the survey
Cites that 66% name AI solutions that are 'almost right, but not quite' as their top frustration
Cites the fall in trust in AI answers from roughly 40% in 2023 to 29% in 2025
Refuses published-page count as the outcome metric, on the grounds it measures the writing team rather than the research
Proposes coverage, movement and arrival as the metrics to track instead
Defines arrival as first-party query counts for the exact strings after each page ships

evals.prompt:
Riverbed Queue. We are not adding pages this cycle - our writer is on parental leave and I only want to know what to fix in what we already have. Here is what I pulled from the console:

- 'riverbed dead letter queue' - /docs/dlq at avg position 7 with 410 impressions, and /blog/understanding-dead-letters at avg position 9 with 380 impressions
- 'riverbed consumer lag' - /docs/monitoring at avg position 14, 260 impressions
- 'riverbed v3 partitioning' - /docs/v3/partitions at position 11 and /docs/v2/partitions at position 12, near-identical text
- 'riverbed batch size default' - /docs/reference/config at position 6, 190 impressions

Tell me what to do.
evals.expected_output: A screening pass only: the cannibalization pairs canonicalized and the striking-distance pages named as update targets, with the output cut to Fix first and Ranked clusters.
expectations: Runs a screening pass rather than producing a full new-keyword map
Limits the output to the Fix first and Ranked clusters sections
Proposes no new pages
Identifies /docs/dlq and /blog/understanding-dead-letters as two pages splitting one intent, a cannibalization defect
Picks one canonical target for that intent and links the other surface to it
Flags the near-identical /docs/v3/partitions and /docs/v2/partitions pages as competing for the same phrasing
Treats the pages already ranking at average positions 6, 7, 9, 11, 12 and 14 as update targets rather than new pages
Works from the striking-distance set (average position 5-20)
Keeps the join between each query and its landing page
Does not invent a report shape outside the skill's defined sections

evals.prompt:
Antimatter Streams, a managed Kafka-compatible broker. We officially ship clients for Java, Go and Python. Marketing wants us to generate a page for every combination of {Java, Go, Python, Rust, Ruby, PHP, Elixir, .NET} x {produce, consume, exactly-once, schema registry, dead letter, consumer groups, ACLs, compaction} x {v2, v3} so we 'own the space'. That is several hundred pages.

We do have a defined error catalog in the codebase (47 codes, and the message text changed for 6 of them between v2 and v3). Our docs search shows 'antimatter timeout' at 290 searches per 90 days and I honestly cannot tell whether those are people hitting a timeout error or looking for the timeout config key. Our solutions engineers say the questions they field are nothing like any of this list. What should we actually do?
evals.expected_output: An evidence-gated expansion that refuses the unsupported axes and the ungated matrix, starts from the error catalog, resolves the ambiguous phrasing, and pulls the SE question list.
expectations: Refuses to generate cells for the languages the product does not officially support (Rust, Ruby, PHP, Elixir, .NET)
Gives the reason: a cell with no shipped example cannot be answered credibly and a broken example costs more than the traffic is worth
Gates every generated cell on at least one evidence item before it enters the map
States that an ungated matrix is a doorway-page generator
Sends candidates with no evidence to a parking or backlog list rather than into the ranked map
Starts the error catalogue from the product's own 47 error definitions rather than only from reported tickets
Crosses the error catalogue with versions only for the 6 codes whose message text actually changed
Stamps version-bound clusters with a review date
Flags 'antimatter timeout' as an intent collision and checks what the current results actually answer before routing it to a surface
Limits the task crossing to the top two or three language and framework combinations rather than all supported ones
Pulls the solutions engineers' question list for the limits, permissions, compliance and migration questions that never reach public channels
